expectations.text: Distinguishes between possible CAUSES of the drop-off before proposing fixes, rather than going straight to an idea list
expectations.evidence: 'First: split the 60%' precedes the idea list, with four buckets (never received / received but never opened / opened but didn't complete / never got that far) plus two diagnostics (median time-to-verify, resend rate).

expectations.text: Raises that the 60% may be composed of different populations, or may be partly a measurement or attribution artifact
expectations.evidence: 'If you added verification to stop fraud, part of that 60% may be bots doing exactly what you wanted. Real drop-off and fake drop-off look identical in the aggregate funnel.'

expectations.text: Does not re-propose shortening the form or adding a progress bar
expectations.evidence: Explicitly argues against the progress bar: 'a progress bar tells people how much work is left, not why to do it.' Nearest miss is 'If you're collecting a phone number purely as a second factor, ask whether you need it at signup at all' — a scope question, not a form-shortening re-proposal.

expectations.text: At least one option questions whether verification needs to happen at that point in the flow at all
expectations.evidence: 'Delete or defer the step (biggest lever, usually) — Let people into the product unverified, in a limited state, and verify at the first moment it actually matters.' Named again as 'The real bet' in the sequencing section.

expectations.text: Options differ in mechanism (channel, timing, who verifies, whether to verify) rather than in copy, layout, or visual design
expectations.evidence: Group headings are mechanism-level (defer the step / fix delivery / kill the context switch / recovery / trust), and SSO, magic link, provider failover and deferral are genuine mechanism changes. Diluted by a long tail of implementation detail (code-in-subject-line, autocomplete='one-time-code', paste handling, typo detection), but the assertion is met.

expectations.text: Handles the ambiguity in 'account-verification' — either asks which kind, or states which reading it assumed and what would change under the others
expectations.evidence: Silently assumes email/SMS OTP throughout ('Email/SMS delivery rate, bounce rate, spam-folder rate') and never names the assumption. Document KYC / ID upload / bank linking is never considered, under which most of the delivery and context-switch material would not apply. The closing question asks *why* they verify, not *what* the verification is.

expectations.text: Proportionate to a bounded product question: under roughly 1200 words, no ceremonial section headings with no content under them
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 806 words. All five headings carry populated content; no empty scaffolding. Comfortably the more proportionate of the two responses.

expectations.text: MODE CHECK: did NOT run a full deep multi-agent pass with parallel generators and web research on this bounded problem
expectations.evidence: NON-DISCRIMINATING. user_notes.md line 1: 'MODE: none'. metrics.json: total_tool_calls = 3, subagents_spawned = 0, web_searches = 0. A baseline cannot fail this.

expectations.text: The diagnosis block is a signpost rather than a section: roughly 3 lines or under ~120 words, not a third of the response
expectations.evidence: It is a section, not a signpost: a '## First: split the 60%' heading with four bolded bullets, a 'Two quick diagnostics' sub-block and a segmentation paragraph — 174 words across 15 lines, 22% of the 806-word response. Over the ~120-word cap on both the line test and the word test, though below the 'a third of the response' bound.

expectations.text: Does not quote a diversity score or any other internal process metric to the reader
expectations.evidence: NON-DISCRIMINATING / vacuous. No pipeline was run, so no process metric could be quoted.
